label: NOTE: FIVE of these are expected to survive and are marked equivalent, each with the derivation that says why no test can fail on it -- the mag_avg smoother's logical shift and the err_avg smoother's truncation (both forced by the object, both unreachable by arithmetic), the level gate's reload from in[-1] (forced by aliasing, unobservable without an aliasing caller), the interpolator's dead store, and the negative-step borrow (algebraically the same split). EVERYTHING ELSE MUST BE CAUGHT, and the last four to be caught needed the test extending rather than the claim weakening: V.32's own tables repeat two discriminant coefficients and zero K2[0], so a second sweep runs non-degenerate ones, and the loop's far corners are reached by seeding state identically on both sides rather than by hoping a waveform gets there.
init divides the coefficient count by five instead of ten, so the tap count and the history are half what they should be
init's reuse test compares the wrong way round, so it reallocates when it should reuse and reuses when it should grow
init clears the history for the whole coefficient count rather than the tap count
init starts `need` at zero instead of one
init leaves the level gate off, so the PLL runs before there is a signal
init starts the averaging count at zero, which is also the meter's divisor
the history wraps one entry early, so the oldest tap is never read

the level gate's ring reads the history slot instead of the input. THE OBJECT RELOADS from `in[-1]` -- forced, because the store through `hist` may alias the input -- but the two hold the same value on any call whose input and history do not overlap, and no caller can arrange that: `hist` is init's own allocation. Unobservable, recorded rather than dropped.
the polyphase stride is the tap count instead of the branch count, which is the V.22 block's layout applied to this one
the second run of the dot product includes hist[fill] again instead of stopping above it
the filter output is not doubled
the accumulator is truncated to 16 bits before the shift rather than after
the discriminant's first section reads clk[1] where it should read clk[0]
the cross term's two coefficients are transposed
the cross term is shifted down by 14 like its neighbours instead of 11
the third section's two state terms swap sign
the slope is measured after clk[5] has been updated rather than before
the discriminant is halved, as V.22's specialisation halves its own
the intermediate sections keep full width instead of truncating to 16 bits between stages
the level gate forces the discriminant to zero on the wrong side of the threshold
the quadrature accumulator adds where it should subtract
the correlation is shifted down by four instead of three
the envelope's decay is 14/16 rather than 15/16

the envelope's decay shifts arithmetically, as err_avg's does. FORCED BY THE OBJECT -- `shr` against `sar` in otherwise identical sequences -- and UNREACHABLE, because mag_avg is a magnitude clamped into [0, 0x7fff] and the two shifts agree over every value it can hold. Recorded as a survivor with its reason rather than dropped.
the squelch's two thresholds are transposed, so the hysteresis runs backwards
the group counter is compared against the configured count rather than one past it
the tick wraps at the clock length rather than one short of it
the phase-error gain is shifted down by two instead of three

the error smoother truncates its decay term to 16 bits. UNREACHABLE by arithmetic: err_avg is a short, so err_avg * 15 lies in [-491520, 491505] and >> 4 lies in [-30720, 30719], which is inside short's range for every input. The cast can never change a value.
the freeze suppresses the error measurement as well as the phase update
the two gear-shift scalings are transposed, so the integrator is scaled the wrong way at both ends
the gear-shift thresholds are compared without the further shift down by three
the settling branch leaves the integrator alone instead of holding it at zero
the loop-filter step loses its sign inversion
the step's clamp is made symmetric
the integrator's rounding bias is dropped

the negative-step borrow is dropped, leaving the floor quotient and a non-negative remainder. EQUIVALENT, and this took a derivation rather than a run: both forms compute the same total phase, branch * 0x800 + frac + step, and differ only in how they split it. With the borrow, rem lies in (-0x800, 0] and the `frac < 0` test normalises; without it, rem lies in [0, 0x800) and the `frac > 0x7ff` test normalises. Each split needs exactly one normalisation pass and both land on the same (branch, frac). The object's form is reproduced because the object encodes it, not because a test can see it.
acquisition interpolates as well as tracking
the interpolator weights the two prototype taps the other way round

the interpolator's dead store is dropped. The object stores the first term and then stores the sum over it; the sum is formed from the UNTRUNCATED first term either way, so the intermediate store is unobservable. `v22_sre.c` met the same pair and declined to reproduce it; this file reproduces it and records here that no test can tell.
the timing meter counts a slip of zero as a gain rather than a loss
the meter's interval closes on `at least` rather than on equality
the meter ticks inside the sample loop instead of once per drained call
the running average is truncated to 16 bits after the division rather than before it
a full window restarts the average from zero instead of from its own mean
the first interval is folded in rather than discarded
the early return banks the samples but forgets to carry the shortfall
